title: DP-4-colorability conjecture for planar graphs without chorded 6-cycles
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and suppose that $G$ contains no chorded $6$-cycle, meaning no cycle of length six with an edge joining two nonconsecutive vertices on the cycle. A graph is **DP-$4$-colorable** if every cover of $G$ admits a DP-coloring with four colors.

**DP-4-colorability conjecture.** Every planar graph without chorded $6$-cycles is DP-$4$-colorable.

The preceding results establish DP-$4$-colorability for a narrower class of planar graphs excluding specified configurations, but the paper does not prove the conjecture for all planar graphs without chorded $6$-cycles.
source_name: Huihui Fang, Danjun Huang, Tao Wang and Weifan Wang, “Variable degeneracy of planar graphs without chorded 6-cycles”, arXiv:2502.18089 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18089

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
